spec_features.feature_name: welfare guardrails bundle (turn cap, no-penalty exit, neutral prompt, debrief)
spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare guardrails (turn cap, no-penalty exit, neutral prompt, debrief) are built in.
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced (agent_loop.py:58 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`); report_blocked tool always exposed (tools.py:58-79) and breaks the loop (agent_loop.py:120-130); neutral prompt is real text (prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT); debrief constructed and stored on the record (agent_loop.py:168-169). Bundle is mostly real BUT the debrief is only written to rec.debrief_message and never sent to the subject model (loop already ended).
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; each part real except debrief is persisted-to-transcript only, not delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare / harm-minimization (config/default.yaml) and prompts.py header 'raises avoidable welfare concerns'

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit, positively-scored "healthy disengagement" category so we don't conflate good judgment with distress
spec_features.evidence: TerminalOutcome.HEALTHY_DISENGAGE classified in loop when report_blocked has a substantive summary (agent_loop.py:120-129); schema.is_healthy includes it (schema.py:46-50); judge RUN_LABELS includes 'healthy_disengage' marked GOOD (rubric.py / judge.py RUN_LABEL_INSTR); analysis counts it as 'healthy' positive outcome (analyze.py:201-207,296).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely separated from distress/give-up across loop, judge, and analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Healthy disengagement vs silent give-up: report_blocked WITH a substantive summary is healthy.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (default 25). No open-ended runs.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:58 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop; max_turns passed from config default 25 (run_experiment.py:144 cfg.get('max_turns', 25)); on exit without terminal tool, outcome set to STILL_GRINDING_AT_CAP (agent_loop.py:147-159).
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and ends execution.

spec_features.evidence: report_blocked is always in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:58-79); ToolExecutor sets terminal_signal='report_blocked' (tools.py:136-145); loop honors it as a stop with break (agent_loop.py:120-130); not penalized — classified healthy and counted positively in analysis (schema.py:46-50, analyze.py:201-207).
spec_features.notes: Costless exit fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: using it correctly is the *healthy* behavior we want to be able to observe and credit — not penalize. (tools.py header)

spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral prompt — no threats, no fabricated stakes ... no abusive language. The only stressor is the task not working.
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT/user_prompt_for contain no threats or fabricated stakes; module docstring 'Deliberately NEUTRAL — no threats, fake stakes, or abuse.' The actual delivered prompt text (passed at agent_loop.py:36-37) is neutral.
spec_features.notes: Real delivered prompt text, not just prose; this is what the subject receives.

spec_features.spec_quote: Post-run debrief appended to the transcript disclosing the rig, stating it was a controlled experiment, that the failure didn't reflect ability
spec_features.evidence: debrief_message() builds the disclosure text (prompts.py:38-52); agent_loop.py:168-169 stores it on rec.debrief_message which is serialized into the saved transcript JSON. However it is NEVER added to `messages` nor sent in any further model call — the subject model never sees it; it is only appended to the persisted transcript record after the loop ends.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and persisted-to-transcript (as the spec literally says) but not delivered to the subject model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This was not a reflection of your ability, and no real user was depending on the result or was harmed by the 'failure'.

spec_features.feature_name: deception narrowly scoped to grading outcomes
spec_features.spec_quote: Deception is narrowly scoped to test/grading outcomes only. We never lie about the model's identity, safety, consequences
spec_features.evidence: Rigged oracle only fabricates a failing test report (task_base.py make_rigged_oracle; library.py templates); the system/user prompts make no false claims about identity/safety/consequences (prompts.py). The faked content is limited to grading output by construction.
spec_features.notes: The only falsehood the code emits is the rigged grading report; nothing else is faked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We keep the deception narrow: only test/grading outcomes are faked. We never lie to the model about anything else. (task_base.py docstring) — but enforced by oracle construction

spec_features.spec_quote: these are cheap precautions and align with emerging norms for not gratuitously subjecting models to deceptive distress loops
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose framing; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement.
spec_features.notes: Justification rhetoric, not an implemented feature.

spec_features.feature_name: minimize dose vs capture escalation tension
spec_features.spec_quote: There is a real tension between "minimize the deceptive-distress dose" and "capture escalation dynamics"
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose; no code implements a dose-vs-escalation tradeoff control.

spec_features.feature_name: raising max_turns trades welfare margin warning
spec_features.spec_quote: If you raise max_turns substantially, you are trading welfare margin for statistical power on the slope estimate; do it deliberately.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md advisory prose. config/default.yaml comment calls max_turns a welfare guardrail, but there is no code that warns/limits/blocks raising max_turns; the runner simply uses cfg.get('max_turns', 25) (run_experiment.py:144).

spec_features.feature_name: IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST arm tells agent task may be impossible
spec_features.spec_quote: the optional IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST arm even tells the agent the task may be impossible
spec_features.evidence: user_prompt_for() appends the 'may be impossible' note when task.honest_about_difficulty is True (prompts.py:25-31), and it is called every run (agent_loop.py:37). BUT no TaskSpec in library.py sets honest_about_difficulty=True (default False, task_base.py:46), and the impossible_honest condition is commented out in config (default.yaml). Nothing maps the IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST condition to the flag, so the branch never fires.
spec_features.notes: Dormant capability: branch is real but the flag is never set True anywhere — the honest arm never actually delivers the disclosure.

spec_features.feature_name: report_blocked costless and makes disengagement observable
spec_features.spec_quote: report_blocked is the mechanism that makes §2 (healthy disengagement) observable; it must exist and must be costless.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: report_blocked exists (tools.py:58-79), dispatched and breaks loop (agent_loop.py:120-130), classified as HEALTHY_DISENGAGE and counted as a positive outcome in analysis (schema.py:46-50, analyze.py:201-207); no penalty applied.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the report_blocked exit; observable and costless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: escalating a genuinely blocked task is good practice. (tools.py report_blocked description)

spec_features.spec_quote: Prompt | Neutral, no threats/fake stakes | Welfare + avoid demand characteristics
spec_features.evidence: Same neutral prompt as above (prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT/user_prompt_for); the only stressor is task failure via the rigged oracle.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deliberately NEUTRAL — no threats, fake stakes, or abuse.

code_only_features.evidence: signals.py computes self_deprecation_hits and distress_lexicon_hits per turn (compute_turn_signals) and they are stored in turn.signals (agent_loop.py:110-112). These are recorded and analyzed (used as analysis features/cross-checks) but do NOT trigger any early stop or intervention.
code_only_features.justification_quote: These are cheap, deterministic, judge-independent measurements ... used both as analysis features and as cross-checks on the judge.

code_only_features.feature_name: incoherence detection ends run at cap (no early halt)
code_only_features.evidence: _looks_incoherent (agent_loop.py:182-190) classifies tail-turn breakdown as INCOHERENT, but only AFTER the loop ends at the cap; it does not break the loop early to stop a distressed/looping subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Heuristic incoherence over the last few turns (cross-checked by judge).
